sentences.zh: 虞玩之

translations.literal: Yu Wanzhi
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wanzhi

sentences.zh: 虞玩之字茂瑤，會稽餘姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Wanzhi, styled Maoyao, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wanzhi, styled Maoyao, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖宗，晉庫部郎。

translations.literal: His ancestor Zong was a Jin storeroom-department gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Zong had been a storeroom-department gentleman under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 父玫，通直常侍。

translations.literal: His father Mei was regular attendant of unimpeded communication.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mei had been regular attendant of unimpeded communication.

sentences.zh: 玩之少閒刀筆，汎涉書史，解褐東海王行參軍，烏程令。

translations.literal: In youth Wanzhi was skilled at clerkly writing, broadly dipped into books and histories, and upon leaving coarse cloth became staff aide to the Prince of Donghai and magistrate of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Wanzhi mastered clerkly writing and ranged widely through books and histories; upon first office he became staff aide to the Prince of Donghai and magistrate of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 路太后外親朱仁彌犯罪，依法錄治。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Lu's maternal kin Zhu Renmi committed a crime; by law he was arrested and prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Lu's maternal kin Zhu Renmi committed a crime; Wanzhi had him arrested and prosecuted by law.

sentences.zh: 太后怨訴孝武，坐免官。

translations.literal: The empress dowager complained to Emperor Xiaowu; he was dismissed from office as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager complained to Emperor Xiaowu; Wanzhi was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，除晉熙國郎中令，尚書起部郎，通直郎。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era he was appointed director of retainers for the Jinxi state, gentleman of the ministry of personnel's promotions section, and unimpeded-attendant gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era he was named director of retainers for Jinxi, gentleman of the ministry of personnel's promotions section, and unimpeded-attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，爲右丞。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era he served as right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhui era he served as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 時太祖參政，與玩之書曰：「張華爲度支尚書，事不徒然。

translations.literal: At the time the founding sovereign held real power in government and wrote to Wanzhi: 「When Zhang Hua served as minister of revenue, his work was not in vain.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the founding sovereign was directing affairs of state and wrote to Wanzhi: 「When Zhang Hua served as minister of revenue, his work was not in vain.

sentences.zh: 今漕藏有闕，吾賢居右丞，已覺金粟可積也。

translations.literal: Now the transport treasuries have gaps; with you, my worthy, in the right vice director's post, I already sense that gold and grain may be piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Now the transport treasuries show gaps; with you, my worthy, as right vice director, I already sense gold and grain may begin to accumulate.

sentences.zh: 」玩之上表陳府庫錢帛，器械役力，所懸轉多，興用漸廣，慮不支歲月。

translations.literal: 」Wanzhi memorialized on the palace treasury's cash, silk, equipment, and labor levies: what hung in suspense grew ever greater, new outlays steadily widened, and he feared the year could not be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wanzhi memorialized that the palace treasury's cash, silk, equipment, and labor levies were ever more entangled in suspense, new outlays steadily widened, and he feared the year could not be sustained.

sentences.zh: 朝議優報之。

translations.literal: Court deliberation gave him a favorable reply.
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberation returned him a favorable reply.

sentences.zh: 遷安成王車騎錄事，轉少府。

translations.literal: He was moved to recorder on the Prince of Ancheng's chariot-and-cavalry staff, then to the lesser treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to recorder on the Prince of Ancheng's chariot-and-cavalry staff, then to the lesser treasury.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮東府，朝野致敬，玩之猶躡屐造席。

translations.literal: When the founding sovereign held the eastern palace, court and countryside paid him homage; Wanzhi still wore clogs and came to his mat.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding sovereign held the eastern palace, court and countryside paid him homage; Wanzhi still wore clogs and came straight to his mat.

sentences.zh: 太祖取屐視之，訛黑斜銳，蒵斷，以芒接之。

translations.literal: The founding sovereign took up the clogs to look at them—worn black, toes slanted and sharp, the vamp split and spliced with straw.
translations.idiomatic: The founding sovereign picked up the clogs to look at them—worn black, toes slanted and sharp, the vamp split and patched with straw.

sentences.zh: 問曰：「卿此屐已幾載？

translations.literal: He asked: 「How many years have you had these clogs?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: 「How many years have you had these clogs?

sentences.zh: 」玩之曰：「初釋褐拜征北行佐買之，著已二十年，貧土竟不辦易。

translations.literal: 」Wanzhi said: 「When I first left coarse cloth and took appointment as northern-campaign staff aide, I bought them; I have worn them twenty years now, and this poor fellow never managed to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wanzhi said: 「When I first took office as northern-campaign staff aide I bought them; I have worn them twenty years, and this poor fellow never managed to replace them.

sentences.zh: 」太祖善之，引爲驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: 」The founding sovereign approved of him and brought him in as fierce-cavalry staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: 」The founding sovereign was pleased with him and brought him in as fierce-cavalry staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 霸府初開，賓客輻湊，太祖留意簡接，玩之與樂安任遐，俱以應對有席上之美，齊名見遇。

translations.literal: When the hegemon's office first opened, guests crowded in like wheel spokes; the founding sovereign took care to choose whom he received. Wanzhi and Ren Xia of Le'an alike won renown for the grace of their table talk and were equally favored.
translations.idiomatic: When the hegemon's office first opened, guests crowded in like wheel spokes; the founding sovereign took care whom he admitted. Wanzhi and Ren Xia of Le'an alike were famed for the grace of their table talk and were equally favored.

sentences.zh: 遐字景遠，好學，有義行，兼與太祖素游，褚淵、王儉竝見親愛。

translations.literal: Xia, styled Jingyuan, loved learning and had a sense of duty; he had long been the founding sovereign's companion, and Chu Yuan and Wang Jian alike held him dear.
translations.idiomatic: Xia, styled Jingyuan, loved learning and had a sense of duty; he had long been the founding sovereign's companion, and Chu Yuan and Wang Jian alike held him dear.

sentences.zh: 官至光祿大夫，永元初卒。

translations.literal: He reached the post of grand master for splendid happiness and died at the opening of Yongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He reached grand master for splendid happiness and died at the opening of Yongyuan.

sentences.zh: 玩之遷驍騎將軍，黃門郎，領本部中正。

translations.literal: Wanzhi was moved to rampant-cavalry general, gentleman of the yellow gate, and concurrently led his home-district rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi was moved to rampant-cavalry general, gentleman of the yellow gate, and concurrently led his home-district rectifier.

sentences.zh: 上患民間欺巧，及卽位，敕玩之與驍騎將軍傅堅意檢定簿籍。

translations.literal: The emperor worried over popular fraud and trickery; upon his accession he ordered Wanzhi and rampant-cavalry general Fu Jianyi to examine and fix the registers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried over popular fraud and trickery; upon his accession he ordered Wanzhi and rampant-cavalry general Fu Jianyi to examine and fix the registers.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，詔朝臣曰：「黃籍，民之大紀，國之治端。

translations.literal: In Jianyuan year 2 he edicted the court ministers: 「The yellow register is the people's great charter and the state's hinge of order.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 2 he edicted the court ministers: 「The yellow register is the people's great charter and the state's hinge of order.

sentences.zh: 自頃氓俗巧偽，爲日已久，至乃竊注爵位，盜易年月，增損三狀，貿襲萬端。

translations.literal: Of late the common folk's cunning fraud has gone on long indeed—to the point of secretly entering noble ranks, stealing and altering birth years, adding or subtracting the three registers, and trading false entries by the myriad.
translations.idiomatic: Of late the common folk's cunning fraud has gone on long indeed—to the point of secretly entering noble ranks, stealing and altering birth years, adding or subtracting the three registers, and trading false entries by the myriad.

sentences.zh: 或戶存而文書已絕，或人在而反託死叛，停私而云隸役，身強而稱六疾。

translations.literal: Some households still exist while their documents are already dead; some men still live while they are recorded as dead or defected; they halt private service yet claim corvée duty; their bodies are strong yet they plead the six illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Some households still exist while their documents are already dead; some men still live while they are recorded as dead or defected; they halt private service yet claim corvée duty; their bodies are strong yet they plead the six illnesses.

sentences.zh: 編戶齊家，少不如此。

translations.literal: Among registered households and ordered families, few are not like this.
translations.idiomatic: Among registered households and ordered families, few are not like this.

sentences.zh: 皆政之巨蠹，教之深疵。

translations.literal: All are great worms in government and deep flaws in teaching.
translations.idiomatic: All are great worms in government and deep flaws in teaching.

sentences.zh: 比年雖卻籍改書，終無得實。

translations.literal: In recent years, though registers were rejected and books altered, in the end the truth was never obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, though registers were rejected and books altered, in the end the truth was never obtained.

sentences.zh: 若約之以刑，則民偽已遠；

translations.literal: If we bind them with punishments, the people's fraud is already far gone;
translations.idiomatic: If we bind them with punishments, the people's fraud is already far gone;

sentences.zh: 若綏之以德，則勝殘未易。

translations.literal: if we soothe them with virtue, transforming the cruel is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: if we soothe them with virtue, transforming the cruel is not easy.

sentences.zh: 卿諸賢竝深明治體，可各獻嘉謀，以振澆化。

translations.literal: You worthies alike are deeply versed in the principles of rule—each may offer a fine plan to rectify shallow customs.
translations.idiomatic: You worthies alike are deeply versed in the principles of rule—each may offer a fine plan to rectify shallow customs.

sentences.zh: 又臺坊訪募，此制不近，優刻素定，閒劇有常。

translations.literal: Again, bureau-yard recruitment: this system is not near at hand; preferential carve-outs were long since fixed, and light and heavy duties have their constants.
translations.idiomatic: Again, bureau-yard recruitment: this system is not near at hand; preferential carve-outs were long since fixed, and light and heavy duties have their constants.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉以前，茲役恆滿，大明以後，樂補稍絕。

translations.literal: Before Liu Song's Yuanjia, this service was always full; after the Daming era, glad substitution gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Before Liu Song's Yuanjia, this service was always full; after the Daming era, glad substitution gradually ceased.

sentences.zh: 或緣寇難頻起，軍蔭易多，民庶從利，投坊者寡。

translations.literal: Sometimes because raids and troubles arose often, military shelter was easily multiplied; the people followed profit, and those who entered the yards were few.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes because raids and troubles arose often, military shelter was easily multiplied; the people followed profit, and those who entered the yards were few.

sentences.zh: 然國經未變，朝紀恆存，相揆而言，隆替何速！

translations.literal: Yet the state's warp was unchanged and the court's warp still stood—measure them against each other: how swift the rise and fall!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the state's warp was unchanged and the court's warp still stood—measure them against each other: how swift the rise and fall!

sentences.zh: 此急病之洪源，晷景之切患，以何科算，革斯弊邪？

translations.literal: This is the great source of acute disease, the pressing ailment of the sundial's shadow—by what statute shall we reckon it and reform this abuse?
translations.idiomatic: This is the great source of acute disease, the pressing ailment of the sundial's shadow—by what statute shall we reckon it and reform this abuse?

sentences.zh: 」玩之上表曰：「宋元嘉二十七年八條取人，孝建元年書籍，衆巧之所始也。

translations.literal: 」Wanzhi memorialized: 「The Yuanjia year 27 eight-article levy of men and the Xiaojian year 1 book-register were where the crowd's tricks began.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wanzhi memorialized: 「The Yuanjia year 27 eight-article levy of men and the Xiaojian year 1 book-register were where the crowd's tricks began.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，故光祿大夫傅隆，年出七十，猶手自書籍，躬加隱校。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era the late grand master for splendid happiness Fu Long, though past seventy, still copied the registers by hand and personally added hidden verification.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era the late grand master for splendid happiness Fu Long, though past seventy, still copied the registers by hand and personally added hidden verification.

sentences.zh: 隆何必有石建之愼，高柔之勤，蓋以世屬休明，服道脩身故耳。

translations.literal: Did Long need Shi Jian's caution or Gao Rou's diligence? It was only that the age belonged to radiant peace and he cultivated the Way and his person.
translations.idiomatic: Did Long need Shi Jian's caution or Gao Rou's diligence? It was only that the age belonged to radiant peace and he cultivated the Way and his person.

sentences.zh: 今陛下日旰忘食，未明求衣，詔逮幽愚，謹陳妄說。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, the sun at the zenith yet forgetting food, seeks his robes before dawn—the edict reaches even this obscure fool; I venture my reckless counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty, the sun at the zenith yet forgetting food, seeks his robes before dawn—the edict reaches even this obscure fool; I venture my reckless counsel.

sentences.zh: 古之共治天下，唯良二千石，今欲求治取正，其在勤明令長。

translations.literal: In antiquity to govern the realm together, only good two-thousand-dan administrators mattered; now if we seek order and take the straight measure, it lies in diligent, clear magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity to govern the realm together, only good two-thousand-dan administrators mattered; now if we seek order and take the straight measure, it lies in diligent, clear magistrates.

sentences.zh: 凡受籍，縣不加檢合，但封送州，州檢得實，方卻歸縣。

translations.literal: Whenever registers were received, the county did not add verification but only sealed and sent them to the province; only when the province's check found truth were they returned to the county.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever registers were received, the county did not add verification but only sealed and sent them to the province; only when the province's check found truth were they returned to the county.

sentences.zh: 吏貪其賂，民肆其姦，姦彌深而卻彌多，賂愈厚而答愈緩。

translations.literal: Clerks greedily took bribes, the people freely practiced fraud—the deeper the fraud, the more rejections; the thicker the bribe, the slower the reply.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks greedily took bribes, the people freely practiced fraud—the deeper the fraud, the more rejections; the thicker the bribe, the slower the reply.

sentences.zh: 自泰始三年至元徽四年，揚州等九郡四號黃籍，共卻七萬一千餘戶。

translations.literal: From Taishi year 3 to Yuanhui year 4, in nine commanderies of Yang province four rounds of yellow-register rejections totaled more than seventy-one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: From Taishi year 3 to Yuanhui year 4, in nine commanderies of Yang province four rounds of yellow-register rejections totaled more than seventy-one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 于今十一年矣，而所正者猶未四萬。

translations.literal: Eleven years have passed since, yet those corrected still fall short of forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven years have passed since, yet those corrected still fall short of forty thousand.

sentences.zh: 神州奧區，尚或如此，江、湘諸部，倍不可念。

translations.literal: In the sacred heartland it is still so; the Jiang and Xiang regions are doubly beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sacred heartland it is still so; the Jiang and Xiang regions are doubly beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜以元嘉二十七年籍爲正。

translations.literal: I humbly hold that the Yuanjia year 27 register should be taken as standard.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hold that the Yuanjia year 27 register should be taken as standard.

sentences.zh: 民惰法旣久，今建元元年書籍，宜更立明科，一聽首悔，迷而不反，依制必戮。

translations.literal: The people have been lax toward the law for a long time; for the Jianyuan year-one register we should establish clear statutes anew, allow all who come forward first to repent, and for those who stray and do not turn back, by regulation they must be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The people have grown lax toward the law for many years; for the Jianyuan year-one register we should lay down clear statutes anew, grant a general amnesty to all who confess first, and execute without mercy those who persist in fraud.

sentences.zh: 使官長審自檢校，必令明洗，然後上州，永以爲正。

translations.literal: Have the magistrates carefully inspect on their own, require that everything be made clear and clean, and only then send up to the prefecture — let that forever be the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates should conduct their own thorough audits, scrub every entry clean, and only then forward the registers to the prefecture — and let that stand as the permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 若有虛昧，州縣同咎。

translations.literal: If anything remains concealed or false, prefecture and county shall share the blame.
translations.idiomatic: Any remaining concealment or falsification shall be punished alike in prefecture and county.

sentences.zh: 今戶口多少，不減元嘉，而板籍頓闕，弊亦有以。

translations.literal: Today the number of households is no less than under Yuanjia, yet the board registers are suddenly depleted — the abuses have their reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Household counts today are no lower than under Yuanjia, yet the board registers have collapsed — and there are clear reasons for the rot.

sentences.zh: 自孝建已來，入勳者衆，其中操干戈衛社稷者，三分殆無一焉。

translations.literal: Since Xiaojian, those entered on the merit rolls have been many; of them, those who bore arms and guarded the altars of state — scarcely one in three.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xiaojian era the merit rolls have swollen with names, yet of those entered scarcely one in three ever bore arms in defense of the realm.

sentences.zh: 勳簿所領而詐注辭籍，浮遊世要，非官長所拘錄，復爲不少。

translations.literal: Merit rolls claimed while registers were fraudulently annotated, drifting among the powerful of the age, beyond what magistrates could seize and record — also not a few.
translations.idiomatic: Men claim merit-book privileges while their household entries are forged, drift among the great families of the day, and escape magistrates' scrutiny — and their number is not small.

sentences.zh: 尋蘇峻平後，庾亮就溫嶠求勳簿，而嶠不與，以爲陶侃所上，多非實錄。

translations.literal: After Su Jun was pacified, Yu Liang asked Wen Qiao for the merit rolls, but Qiao would not give them, holding that what Tao Kan had submitted was largely not a true record.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun's defeat, Yu Liang asked Wen Qiao for the merit rolls, but Qiao refused, saying Tao Kan's submissions were largely fictitious.

sentences.zh: 尋物之懷私，無世不有，宋末落紐，此巧尤多。

translations.literal: Seeking gain with a private heart — no age lacks it; at the end of Song the reins slackened, and this trickery was especially rife.
translations.idiomatic: Self-seeking has never been absent in any age; but when Song neared its fall the bonds loosened, and this sort of fraud flourished as never before.

sentences.zh: 又將位旣衆，舉卹爲祿，實潤甚微，而人領數萬，如此二條，天下合役之身，已據其太半矣。

translations.literal: Also, general ranks are already numerous; mourning stipends are raised as salary, yet the actual benefit is very slight, while men draw stipends in the tens of thousands — these two items alone already account for more than half of all conscripted bodies in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Generalships have multiplied, men claim mourning stipends as salary though the real gain is trifling, and thousands draw pay under each title — these two abuses alone already consume more than half the empire's conscriptable manpower.

sentences.zh: 又有改注籍狀。

translations.literal: There is also the altering of registered household status.
translations.idiomatic: Registers are also altered wholesale.

sentences.zh: 詐入仕流，昔爲人役者，今反役人。

translations.literal: Fraudulently entering the official class — once men's servants, now in turn they enslave others.
translations.idiomatic: Men fraudulently enter the official class: yesterday they served others; today they command servants of their own.

sentences.zh: 又生不長髮，便謂爲道人，塡街溢巷，是處皆然。

translations.literal: Also, those who from birth do not grow hair are at once called Daoist priests — filling the streets and overflowing the alleys; everywhere it is so.
translations.idiomatic: Men who never grow hair declare themselves Daoist priests and fill every street and alley — the same fraud in every district.

sentences.zh: 或抱子幷居，竟不編戶，遷徙去來，公違土斷。

translations.literal: Some hold their children and live together yet never register as households; they migrate back and forth and openly violate the land-allotment statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Some live with wives and children yet never register a household, roaming from place to place in open defiance of the land-allotment laws.

sentences.zh: 屬役無滿，流亡不歸，寧喪終身，疾病長臥。

translations.literal: Attached service goes unfulfilled; exiles do not return; they would rather die in exile than come home, or lie abed with chronic illness.
translations.idiomatic: Conscripts fail to report for service; exiles refuse to return; some would rather die abroad than obey summons, others plead chronic illness and never rise.

sentences.zh: 法令必行，自然競反。

translations.literal: If laws and orders are truly enforced, men will naturally compete to return.
translations.idiomatic: Enforce the statutes in earnest and men will rush to comply of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 又四鎮戍將，有名寡實，隨才部曲，無辨勇懦，署位借給，巫媼比肩，彌山滿海，皆是私役。

translations.literal: Also the four frontier garrison generals: names many, substance few; retainers taken at whim with no distinction of brave or coward; posts lent out on paper; shamans shoulder to shoulder, filling mountains and seas — all are private servants.
translations.idiomatic: The four frontier garrison generals too keep grand titles and empty ranks, enroll retainers without testing courage or cowardice, lend out offices on paper, and surround themselves with shamans and sorceresses mountain-high and sea-wide — all private servants, every one.

sentences.zh: 行貨求位，其塗甚易，募役卑劇，何爲投補？

translations.literal: Bribery wins a post — the path is very easy; conscript service is base and harsh — why throw oneself in to fill the rolls?
translations.idiomatic: A bribe buys a commission with ease, while conscript duty is mean and brutal — why would anyone volunteer to fill the ward rolls?

sentences.zh: 坊吏之所以盡，百里之所以單也。

translations.literal: This is why ward clerks are exhausted and hundred-li districts stand empty.
translations.idiomatic: That is why ward clerks are run to exhaustion and districts lie stripped of men.

sentences.zh: 今但使募制明信，滿復有期，民無逕路，則坊可立表而盈矣。

translations.literal: Now if only the conscription system were made trustworthy and clear, fulfillment and restoration were given a fixed term, and the people had no side path, then the wards could post their rosters and be full again.
translations.idiomatic: Make the conscription system transparent and binding, set a fixed term for fulfillment and release, and close every loophole — then the wards can post full rosters once more.

sentences.zh: 爲治不患無制，患在不行，不患不行，患在不久。

translations.literal: In governing one does not fear lacking systems; one fears they are not carried out. One does not fear they are not carried out; one fears they will not last.
translations.idiomatic: Good government is not undone by want of rules but by failure to enforce them; not by failure to enforce them but by failure to persevere.

sentences.zh: 」上省玩之表，納之。

translations.literal: 」The emperor reviewed Wanzhi's memorial and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor reviewed Wanzhi's memorial and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 乃別置板籍官，置令史，限人一日得數巧，以防懈怠。

translations.literal: Thereupon a separate board-register office was set up with clerks, each man limited to uncovering several frauds in a day, to guard against laxity.
translations.idiomatic: A separate board-register office was established with clerks, each required to expose a set quota of frauds per day lest they grow slack.

sentences.zh: 於是貨賂因緣，籍注雖正，猶強推卻，以充程限。

translations.literal: Then bribes worked through connections; though the register entries were correct, they were still forcibly rejected to meet the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Bribes soon bought exemption; even honest entries were forced back into dispute so clerks could meet their daily quota.

sentences.zh: 至世祖永明八年，謫巧者戍緣淮各十年，百姓怨望。

translations.literal: By the eighth year of Yongming under Emperor Shizu, those convicted of registry fraud were banished to garrison the Huai frontier for ten years each, and the people groaned with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming, Emperor Wu banished registry fraudsters to garrison the Huai frontier for ten years apiece, and popular resentment boiled over.

sentences.zh: 世祖乃詔曰：「夫簡貴賤，辨尊卑者，莫不取信於黃籍。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued an edict: 「In sorting noble from base and distinguishing high from low, all take their trust from the yellow register.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then decreed: 「Rank and station rest on the yellow register;

sentences.zh: 豈有假器濫榮，竊服非分。

translations.literal: How could one borrow titles and abuse honor, steal rank beyond one's measure?
translations.idiomatic: how could men borrow titles, abuse honors, and usurp rank beyond their due?

sentences.zh: 故所以澄革虛妄，式允舊章。

translations.literal: Therefore we clarify and reform the false, to accord with the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: We purge the false and restore the old statutes.

sentences.zh: 然釁起前代，過非近失，旣往之諐，不足追咎。

translations.literal: Yet the taint arose in former ages; the fault is not a recent slip. Wrongs already past are not worth pursuing to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these abuses arose in earlier reigns, not in yesterday's lapse; past wrongs shall not be punished retroactively.

sentences.zh: 自宋昇明以前，皆聽復注。

translations.literal: Before Shengming of Song, all are permitted to re-register.
translations.idiomatic: All who registered before Song's Shengming era may re-enter the rolls.

sentences.zh: 其有謫役邊疆，各許還本。

translations.literal: Those banished to frontier service are each permitted to return to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: Those banished to frontier labor may each return home.

sentences.zh: 此後有犯，嚴加翦治。」

translations.literal: After this, offenders shall be sternly cut down and disciplined.」
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, offenders shall be punished without leniency.」

sentences.zh: 玩之以久宦衰疾，上表告退，曰：「臣聞負重致遠，力窮則困，竭誠事君，智盡必傾，理固然也。

translations.literal: Wanzhi, long in office and worn by illness, submitted a memorial asking to retire, saying: 「Your servant has heard that he who bears a heavy load on a long road, when strength is spent, is trapped; he who serves his lord with utmost loyalty, when wisdom is exhausted, must lean — such is the way of things.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi, worn out by long service and illness, asked to retire, writing: 「I have heard that a man who bears a heavy load on a long road is trapped when his strength fails; a man who serves his lord with all his heart must lean when his wit is spent — such is the way of things.

sentences.zh: 四十仕進，七十懸車，壯則驅馳，老宜休息。

translations.literal: At forty one enters office; at seventy one hangs up the carriage — in strength one drives on, in age one should rest.
translations.idiomatic: At forty one takes office; at seventy one hangs up the carriage — youth may drive on, age should rest.

sentences.zh: 臣生於晉，長於宋，老於齊，世歷三代，朝市再易。

translations.literal: Your servant was born under Jin, grew up under Song, and grows old under Qi — three dynasties in one life, the court and market twice transformed.
translations.idiomatic: I was born under Jin, grew up under Song, and grow old under Qi — three dynasties in one lifetime, two overturnings of throne and market.

sentences.zh: 臣以宋元嘉二十八年爲王府行佐，於茲三十年矣。

translations.literal: Your servant in the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia of Song became staff aide to a princely establishment — thirty years have passed since.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia I became staff aide to a princely household — thirty years have passed since.

sentences.zh: 自頃以來，衰耗漸篤。

translations.literal: In recent times decline and exhaustion have grown severe.
translations.idiomatic: Of late my decline has grown steep.

sentences.zh: 爲性不懶惰，而倦怠頓來。

translations.literal: By nature I am not lazy, yet weariness has suddenly come on.
translations.idiomatic: I am not lazy by nature, yet exhaustion has seized me all at once.

sentences.zh: 耳目本聰明，而聾矒轉積。

translations.literal: Ears and eyes were once keen, yet deafness and dimness have steadily piled up.
translations.idiomatic: My ears and eyes were once sharp; now deafness and dim sight mount day by day.

sentences.zh: 腳不支身，喘不緒氣。

translations.literal: The feet cannot support the body; the breath cannot thread the qi.
translations.idiomatic: My legs will not bear me; my breath comes in broken gasps.

sentences.zh: 景刻不推，朝晝不保。

translations.literal: The sun's shadow will not advance; morning and noon are not assured.
translations.idiomatic: The sundial's shadow scarcely moves; I cannot count on seeing another noon.

sentences.zh: 大功兄弟，四十有二人，通塞壽夭，唯臣獨存。

translations.literal: Brothers of the same great-grief mourning grade, forty-two in all — through fortune and misfortune, long life and early death, only your servant remains.
translations.idiomatic: Of forty-two brothers who shared the deepest mourning bond, through fortune and ruin, long life and early death, I alone remain.

sentences.zh: 朝露末光，寧堪長久！

translations.literal: Morning dew's last gleam — how could it endure long!
translations.idiomatic: I am morning dew at its last gleam — how could I endure?

sentences.zh: 且知足不辱，臣已足矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, he who knows sufficiency is not shamed — your servant has had enough.
translations.idiomatic: And he who knows when he has enough is not disgraced — I have had enough.

sentences.zh: 稟命饑寒，不求富貴，銅山由命，臣何恨焉，久甘之矣。

translations.literal: Heaven's allotment is hunger and cold; I do not seek wealth and honor. Copper mountains lie in fate's hand — what resentment could your servant harbor? Long I have been content.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gave me hunger and cold, not wealth; whether fate grants a copper mountain or not, I bear no grudge — I have been content long since.

sentences.zh: 直道事人，不免縲紲，屬遇聖明，知其非罪，臣之幸厚矣。

translations.literal: Serving men on the straight path, I could not escape the halter; meeting a sage reign, the court knew I was not guilty — your servant's fortune was already great.
translations.idiomatic: Serving others on the straight path I could not escape the halter; under a sage reign the court knew my innocence — my fortune was already great.

sentences.zh: 授命於道消之晨，效節於百揆之日，臣忠之效也。

translations.literal: Receiving mandate in the dawn when the Way declined, showing loyalty on the day when all chiefs gathered — that was your servant's effect of loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: I took office as the Jin Way faded, and served faithfully when the hundred offices were first assembled — that was my loyalty fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 降慶於文明之初，荷澤於天飛之運，臣命之偶也。

translations.literal: Blessing descended at the opening of Wenming, favor was borne on the fortune of heaven's flight — that was your servant's chance of fate.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing came at the opening of Wenming; I bore favor in the fortune of the dynasty's rise — that was my lot in fate.

sentences.zh: 不謀巧宦而位至九卿，德慙李陵而忝居門下。

translations.literal: Without scheming for clever office I reached the nine ministers; in virtue I am ashamed before Li Ling, yet I occupy a post at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Without scheming for preferment I rose to the nine ministers; in virtue I am no Li Ling, yet I hold a post at the gate.

sentences.zh: 堯舜無窮，臣亦通矣。

translations.literal: Yao and Shun are without end — your servant too has passed through.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun's blessings know no end — and I too have passed through them.

sentences.zh: 年過六十，不爲夭矣。

translations.literal: Past sixty years — that is not an early death.
translations.idiomatic: Past sixty — that is no early death.

sentences.zh: 榮期之三樂，東平之一善，臣俱盡之矣。

translations.literal: Rongqi's three joys and Dongping's one virtue — your servant has attained them all.
translations.idiomatic: Rongqi's three joys and Dongping's one good deed — I have attained them all.

sentences.zh: 經昏踐亂，涉艱履危，仰聖德以求全，憑賢輔以申節，未嘗厭屈於勳權，畏溺於狐鼠，臣立身之本，於斯不虧。

translations.literal: Having passed through dark reigns and trampled chaos, forded hardship and walked on danger, I looked up to sage virtue to keep myself whole and leaned on worthy aides to hold my measure; I never tired of bending before merit and power, never feared drowning among foxes and rats—the ground on which I stand has not cracked here.
translations.idiomatic: I passed through dark reigns and trampled chaos, forded hardship and walked on danger; I looked up to sage virtue to keep myself whole and leaned on worthy aides to hold my station. I never tired of bending before merit and power, never feared drowning among foxes and rats—yet the ground I stand on has not given way.

sentences.zh: 在其壯也，當官不讓；

translations.literal: In my prime I would not yield an office;
translations.idiomatic: In my strength I would not yield an office;

sentences.zh: 及其衰矣，豪露靡因。

translations.literal: in my decline, swagger and display have nothing left to lean on.
translations.idiomatic: in my waning years, swagger and show have nothing left to lean on.

sentences.zh: 伏願慈臨，賜臣骸骨。

translations.literal: I humbly beg your kindness to look upon me and grant me my bones.
translations.idiomatic: I bow low and beg your kindness to look upon me and grant me my bones.

sentences.zh: 非爲希高慕古，愛好泉林，特以丁運孤貧，養禮多闕，風樹之感，夙自纏心。

translations.literal: Not that I court loftiness or pine for forests and springs—only that fate left me solitary and poor, my rites of nurture much broken; the wind-and-tree grief has gnawed at me since long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Not that I court loftiness or pine for forests and springs—only that fate left me solitary and poor, my rites of nurture much broken; the wind-and-tree grief has gnawed at me since long ago.

sentences.zh: 庶天假其辰，得二三年間，掃守丘墓，以此歸全，始終之報遂矣。

translations.literal: May Heaven lend me a span—two or three years—to sweep and keep my parents' mound; thus I may return whole, and my debt from first to last be paid.
translations.idiomatic: May Heaven lend me a span—two or three years—to sweep and keep my parents' mound; thus I may return whole, and my debt from first to last be paid.

sentences.zh: 」上省玩之表，許之。

translations.literal: 」The emperor reviewed Wan's memorial and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: 」The throne read Wan's memorial and granted it.

sentences.zh: 玩之於人物好臧否。

translations.literal: Wan was fond of judging people, for good or ill.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was keen to judge men, for good or ill.

sentences.zh: 宋末，王儉舉員外郎孔襜使虜，玩之言論不相饒，襜、儉竝恨之。

translations.literal: Late in Song, Wang Jian recommended Outer Court Gentleman Kong Can as envoy to the north; Wan's remarks showed no mercy, and Can and Jian both hated him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Song, Wang Jian recommended Outer Court Gentleman Kong Can as envoy to the north; Wan's remarks showed no mercy, and Can and Jian both hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 至是玩之東歸，儉不出送，朝廷無祖餞者。

translations.literal: When Wan returned east, Jian did not come out to see him off; the court held no farewell feast for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan went home east, Jian would not come out to see him off; the court held no farewell for him.

sentences.zh: 玩之歸家起大宅，數年卒。

translations.literal: Wan returned home and raised a great mansion; within a few years he died.
translations.idiomatic: Wan raised a great house at home and died within a few years.

sentences.zh: 其後員外郎孔瑄就儉求會稽五官，儉方盥，投皂莢於地，曰：「卿鄉俗惡。

translations.literal: Later Outer Court Gentleman Kong Xuan asked Jian for the Five Offices in Kuaiji; Jian was at his washstand and flung his soap pod to the floor, saying: 「The ways of your homeland are foul.
translations.idiomatic: Later Outer Court Gentleman Kong Xuan asked Jian for the Five Offices in Kuaiji; Jian was at his washstand and flung his soap pod to the floor, saying: 「The ways of your homeland are foul.

sentences.zh: 虞玩之至死煩人。」

translations.literal: Yu Wanzhi was a pest to the very end.」
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wanzhi was a pest to the very end.」

sentences.zh: 孔襜字世遠，玩之同郡人，好典故學。

translations.literal: Kong Can, styled Shiyuan, was Wan's fellow townsman and loved learning in statutes and precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Can, styled Shiyuan, was Wan's fellow townsman and doted on statutes and precedent.

sentences.zh: 與王儉至交。

translations.literal: He and Wang Jian were close friends.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wang Jian were fast friends.

sentences.zh: 昇明中爲齊臺尚書儀曹郎，太祖謂之曰：「卿儀曹才也。

translations.literal: In Shengming he served the Qi headquarters as Director of Ceremonial in the Secretariat; the Grand Ancestor told him: 「You are Ceremonies Office talent.」
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming he served the Qi headquarters as Director of Ceremonial in the Secretariat; the Grand Ancestor told him: 「You are Ceremonies Office talent.」

sentences.zh: 」儉爲宰相，襜嘗謀議帷幕，每及選用，頗失鄉曲情。

translations.literal: When Jian was chief minister, Can often counseled behind the curtain; whenever appointments arose, he often slighted hometown ties.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian was chief minister, Can often counseled behind the curtain; whenever appointments arose, he often slighted hometown ties.

sentences.zh: 儉從容啓上曰：「臣有孔襜，猶陛下之有臣也。

translations.literal: Jian calmly told the throne: 「Your servant has Kong Can, as Your Majesty has your servant.」
translations.idiomatic: Jian calmly told the throne: 「Your servant has Kong Can, as Your Majesty has your servant.」

sentences.zh: 」永明中爲太子家令，卒。

translations.literal: In Yongming he was Heir Apparent Household Steward; he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming he was Heir Apparent Household Steward; he died.

sentences.zh: 時人呼孔襜、何憲爲王儉三公。

translations.literal: Men of the day called Kong Can and He Xian the three dukes at Wang Jian's side.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the day called Kong Can and He Xian the three dukes at Wang Jian's side.
