translations.idiomatic: Appended: He Xian

sentences.zh: 憲字子思，廬江人也。

translations.literal: He Xian, styled Zisi, was of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Xian, styled Zisi, was of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 以強學見知。

translations.literal: He was known for forceful, wide learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for forceful, wide learning.

sentences.zh: 母鎮北長史王敷之女，聰明有訓識。

translations.literal: His mother was a daughter of Pacification Army Chief Clerk Wang Fu—bright, and trained in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a daughter of Pacification Army Chief Clerk Wang Fu—bright, and trained in judgment.

sentences.zh: 憲爲本州別駕。

translations.literal: He held Vice Prefect of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: He held Vice Prefect of his home province.

sentences.zh: 永明十年，使于虜中。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming he was sent as envoy among the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongming he was sent as envoy among the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 劉休

translations.literal: Liu Xiu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiu

sentences.zh: 劉休字弘明，沛郡相人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiu, styled Hongming, came from Xiang in Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiu, styled Hongming, came from Xiang in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖徽，正員郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui was Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 父超，九眞太守。

translations.literal: His father Chao was Administrator of Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chao was Administrator of Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 休初爲駙馬都尉，奉朝請，宋明帝湘東國常侍。

translations.literal: Xiu first served as Commandant of the Horse Fleet, Court Attendant for Imperial Audiences, and regular attendant in Prince Xiangdong's establishment under Emperor Ming of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu first served as Commandant of the Horse Fleet, Court Attendant for Imperial Audiences, and regular attendant in Prince Xiangdong's establishment under Emperor Ming of Song.

sentences.zh: 好學諳憶，不爲帝所知。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had a retentive memory, yet the emperor did not know him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and had a retentive memory, yet the emperor did not know him.

sentences.zh: 襲祖封南鄉侯。

translations.literal: He inherited his grandfather's fief as Marquis of Nanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his grandfather's fief as Marquis of Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 友人陳郡謝儼同丞相義宣反，休坐匿之，被繫尚方七年，孝武崩，乃得出。

translations.literal: His friend Xie Yan of Chen joined Chancellor Yixuan's rebellion; Xiu was convicted of hiding him and held in the Imperial Workshop seven years, coming out only when Emperor Xiaowu died.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Xie Yan of Chen joined Chancellor Yixuan's rebellion; Xiu was convicted of hiding him and held in the Imperial Workshop seven years, coming out only when Emperor Xiaowu died.

sentences.zh: 隨弟欽爲羅縣。

translations.literal: He followed his younger brother Qin to Luo county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his younger brother Qin to Luo county.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，諸州反，休筮明帝當勝，靜處不預異謀。

translations.literal: In early Taishi, when the provinces rose in revolt, Xiu divined that Emperor Ming would prevail and kept apart, taking no part in the plotters.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taishi, when the provinces rose in revolt, Xiu divined that Emperor Ming would prevail and kept apart, taking no part in the plotters.

sentences.zh: 數年，還投吳喜爲輔師府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: After several years he returned and entered Wu Xi's staff as recorder in the Supporting Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he returned and entered Wu Xi's staff as recorder in the Supporting Army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 喜稱其才，進之明帝，得在左右。

translations.literal: Xi praised his gifts and recommended him to Emperor Ming; he won a place at the sovereign's side.
translations.idiomatic: Xi praised his gifts and recommended him to Emperor Ming; he won a place at the sovereign's side.

sentences.zh: 板桂陽王征北參軍。

translations.literal: He was commissioned Northern Campaign aide to the Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was commissioned Northern Campaign aide to the Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 帝頗有好尚，尤嗜飲食。

translations.literal: The emperor had many pursuits, above all food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had many pursuits, above all food and drink.

sentences.zh: 休多藝能，爰及鼎味，問無不解。

translations.literal: Xiu had many arts, down to cauldrons and flavors—ask him anything, and he answered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had many arts, down to cauldrons and flavors—ask him anything, and he answered.

sentences.zh: 後宮孕者，帝使筮其男女，無不如占。

translations.literal: When women of the rear palace were with child, the emperor had him divine boy or girl; he never missed.
translations.idiomatic: When women of the rear palace were with child, the emperor had him divine boy or girl; he never missed.

sentences.zh: 帝素肥，痿不能御內，諸王妓妾懷孕，使密獻入宮，生子之後，閉其母於幽房，前後十數。

translations.literal: The emperor was naturally heavy and impotent, unable to attend the inner quarters; when singing girls and concubines of the princes grew pregnant, he had them brought secretly into the palace, and after the birth shut the mothers in secluded rooms—more than ten such cases in all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was by nature stout and impotent, unable to attend the inner quarters; when princes' singing girls and concubines grew with child, he had them smuggled into the palace, and after the birth walled the mothers in secluded rooms—a dozen such cases and more.

sentences.zh: 順帝，桂陽王休範子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun was the son of the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun was the son of the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王亦非帝子，陳太妃先爲李道兒妾，故蒼梧微行，嘗自稱爲李郎焉。

translations.literal: The Prince of Cangwu was also not the emperor's son: Grand Consort Chen had first been Li Dao'er's concubine, and so the Prince of Cangwu, in private dress, once called himself Lord Li.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Cangwu was also not the emperor's son: Grand Consort Chen had first been Li Dao'er's concubine, and so the Prince of Cangwu, in private dress, once called himself Lord Li.

sentences.zh: 帝憎婦人妒，尚書右丞榮彥遠以善棊見親，婦妒傷其面，帝曰：「我爲卿治之，何如？

translations.literal: The emperor detested jealous wives; Vice Director of the Secretariat Rong Yanyuan was prized for skill at chess, and his wife's jealousy marred his face. The emperor said: 「I shall cure that for you—how would you like it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor detested jealous wives; Vice Director of the Secretariat Rong Yanyuan was prized for skill at chess, and his wife's jealousy marred his face. The emperor said: 「I shall cure that for you—how would you like it?

sentences.zh: 」彥遠率爾應曰：「聽聖旨。

translations.literal: 」Yan Yuan offhand replied: 「I hear Your Majesty's command.
translations.idiomatic: 」Yan Yuan answered without thinking, 「As Your Majesty wills.」

sentences.zh: 」其夕，遂賜藥殺其妻。

translations.literal: 」That same evening, medicine was bestowed to kill his wife.
translations.idiomatic: 」That very night the emperor sent poison and had his wife killed.

sentences.zh: 休妻王氏亦妒，帝聞之，賜休妾，敕與王氏二十杖。

translations.literal: Xiu's wife, the Wang clan, was also jealous; the emperor heard of it, bestowed Xiu a concubine, and ordered twenty strokes for Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's wife Wang was jealous too; when the emperor heard, he gave Xiu a concubine and ordered Wang beaten twenty times.

sentences.zh: 令休於宅後開小店，使王氏親賣掃帚皂莢以辱之。

translations.literal: He ordered Xiu to open a small shop behind his residence and made Wang personally sell brooms and soap pods to humiliate her.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xiu open a little shop behind the house and made Wang sell brooms and soap pods herself, to shame her.

sentences.zh: 其見親如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: That was how close he stood to the throne.

sentences.zh: 尋除員外郎，領輔國司馬、中書通事舍人，帶南城令。

translations.literal: Soon he was made aide, with concurrent aide to the Pacification Army, secretariat communication attendant, and Intendant of Southern City.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made an aide, with concurrent posts as Pacification Army aide, secretariat communication attendant, and intendant of Southern City.

sentences.zh: 除尚書中兵郎，給事中，舍人、令如故。

translations.literal: He was made Secretariat Central Troops Officer and attendant at the bureau; attendant and intendant stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made secretariat central troops officer and attendant at the bureau; his attendant and intendant posts were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 除安成王撫軍參軍，出爲都水使者，南康相。

translations.literal: He was made staff officer to the Prince of Ancheng's Pacification Army, then sent out as Commissioner of Waters and Chancellor of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made staff officer on the Prince of Ancheng's pacification army, then sent out as commissioner of waters and chancellor of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 休善言治體，而在郡無異績。

translations.literal: Xiu spoke well on governing principles, but in the commandery achieved nothing distinctive.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu talked fluently about how states should be run, yet in office he left no mark worth naming.

sentences.zh: 還爲正員郎，邵陵王南中郎錄事、建威將軍、新蔡太守。

translations.literal: He returned as a regular officer, Prince of Shaoling's Southern Center Staff recorder, Jianwei general, and Grand Administrator of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: He came back as a regular officer, recorder on the Prince of Shaoling's southern staff, Jianwei general, and grand administrator of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 隨轉左軍府，加鎮蠻護軍，將軍、太守如故。

translations.literal: He transferred with the Left Army headquarters, was given the added title Pacification of the Barbarians Protector-General; general and grand administrator stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He moved with the left army headquarters and was given the added title protector-general for pacifying the barbarians; his generalship and grand administration stayed the same.

sentences.zh: 遷諮議，司馬，進寧朔將軍，鎮蠻護軍、太守如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to adviser and military aide, advanced to Ningshuo general; Pacification of the Barbarians and grand administrator stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to adviser and military aide and advanced to Ningshuo general; his barbarian-pacification and grand administration posts were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 徙尋陽太守，將軍、司馬如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand Administrator of Xunyang; general and military aide stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand administrator of Xunyang; his generalship and military aide post remained.

sentences.zh: 後遷長史。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to chief aide.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made chief aide.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之難，世祖挾晉熙邵陵二王軍府鎮盆城，休承奉軍費，事寧，仍遷邵陵王安南長史，除黃門郎，寧朔將軍，前軍長史，齊臺散騎常侍。

translations.literal: During Shen Youzhi's rebellion, Emperor Xiaowu seized the military headquarters of the two princes at Pencheng; Xiu managed military expenses; when the matter was settled, he was moved to the Prince of Shaoling's Pacification of the South chief aide, made Yellow Gate Officer, Ningshuo general, front army chief aide, and Qi Platform Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rose, Emperor Xiaowu took the joint army headquarters of the princes at Pencheng; Xiu handled military funds. After peace returned he became the Prince of Shaoling's pacification-of-the-south chief aide, then yellow gate officer, Ningshuo general, front-army chief aide, and Qi platform regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 建元初，爲御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the opening of Jianyuan he was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianyuan began he was made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 頃之，休啓曰：「臣自塵榮南憲，星晷交春，謬聞弱奏，劾無空月。

translations.literal: Before long Xiu memorialized, saying: 「Since I took office stained by southern censorial glory, stars and seasons have crossed spring; weak reports were wrongly heard, and impeachments never left a month empty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Xiu memorialized: 「Since I took this southern censor's seat, a year has turned; feeble denunciations were credited, and not one month passed without an impeachment.

sentences.zh: 豈唯不能使蕃邦斂手，豪右屏氣，乃遣聽已暴之辜，替網觸羅之鳥。

translations.literal: Not only could I not make frontier states fold their hands and powerful houses hold their breath, I even sent forth those who listened to guilt already exposed, birds that brushed the net in another's place.
translations.idiomatic: I could not even make the borderlands stand down or the great houses quail; I only turned loose men who heard out crimes already plain, and birds that had touched the net in someone else's stead.

sentences.zh: 而猶以此，里失鄉黨之和，朝絕比肩之顧，覆背騰其喉唇，武人厲其觜吻。

translations.literal: Yet because of this, hamlets lost neighborhood harmony, the court lost shoulder-to-shoulder regard; turncoats raised throat and lips, military men whet beak and mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, villages lost the peace of the lane, the court lost the glance of equals; back-turners filled the air with accusation, and soldiers sharpened their tongues for attack.

sentences.zh: 怨之所聚，勢難久堪；

translations.literal: Where resentment gathers, the situation is hard to bear long;
translations.idiomatic: Where hatred pools, no man can stand it for long;

sentences.zh: 議之所裁，孰懷其允？

translations.literal: where deliberation cuts, who holds its fairness?
translations.idiomatic: where judgment falls, who believes it just?

sentences.zh: 臣竊尋宋世載祀六十，歷職斯任者五十有三，校其年月，不過盈歲。

translations.literal: I privately trace the Song age's sixty years of sacrifice: fifty-three men held this office; compare their years and months, and none exceeded a full year.
translations.idiomatic: I have looked back through the Song's sixty reign-years: fifty-three men held this post, and none of them, by the count of years and months, lasted more than one.

sentences.zh: 于臣叨濫，宜請骸骨。

translations.literal: As for my presumptuous excess, I should request bones and flesh.
translations.idiomatic: For my own presumption, I ought to ask leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿職當國司，以威裁爲本，而忽憚世誚。

translations.literal: 」The emperor said: 「Your office stands as national inspector; awe and judgment are its foundation—yet you suddenly fear worldly ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor said, 「Your post is the state's inspector; its root is awe and judgment—yet now you flinch at the world's mockery.

sentences.zh: 卿便應辭之事始，何可獲惰晚節邪？」

translations.literal: You should have resigned at the start; how can you slack into a lazy late season?」
translations.idiomatic: You should have quit when you began. How can you coast into a soft old age?」

sentences.zh: 宋末，上造指南車，以休有思理，使與王僧虔對共監試。

translations.literal: At the end of Song the emperor built a south-pointing chariot; because Xiu had reflective mind, he had him with Wang Sengqian jointly supervise the trial.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Song the throne built a south-pointing carriage; finding Xiu thoughtful, the emperor set him with Wang Sengqian to oversee the test together.

sentences.zh: 元嘉世，羊欣受子敬正隸法，世共宗之，右軍之體微古，不復見貴。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era Yang Xin received Zi Jing's orthodox clerical method; the age together honored it; the Right General's style was slightly archaic and no longer prized.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuankang, Yang Xin took up Zi Jing's standard clerical hand and the world bowed to it; the Right General's manner, a little old-fashioned, was no longer valued.

sentences.zh: 休始好此法，至今此體大行。

translations.literal: Xiu first loved this method; to this day this style greatly prevails.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was the first to favor that school; even now it rules the field.

sentences.zh: 四年，出爲豫章內史，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was sent out as Intendant of Yuzhang, with the added title Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he went out as intendant of Yuzhang, with champion general added to his name.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 沈沖

translations.literal: Shen Chong
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong

sentences.zh: 沈沖字景綽，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Chong styled Jingchuo and was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong, styled Jingchuo, came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖宣，新安太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuan was Grand Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan had been grand administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 父懷文，廣陵太守。

translations.literal: His father Huaiwen was Grand Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huaiwen had been grand administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 沖解褐衛尉五官，轉揚州主簿。

translations.literal: Chong began office as Five Officials of the Guard Commandant and transferred to Yangzhou chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Chong entered service as five officials under the guard commandant, then became Yangzhou chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 宋大明中，懷文有文名，沖亦涉獵文義。

translations.literal: In Song's Daming period Huaiwen had literary fame, and Chong also ranged in literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's Daming reign Huaiwen won a name for letters, and Chong too dipped into literary studies.

sentences.zh: 轉西陽王撫軍法曹參軍，尋舉秀才，還爲撫軍正佐，兼記室。

translations.literal: He transferred to Prince of Xiyang's Pacification Army Law Cao staff officer, was soon nominated as xiucai, and returned as Pacification Army principal aide, also secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He became law-cao staff officer on the Prince of Xiyang's pacification army, was soon nominated as xiucai, and came back as the army's principal aide, doubling as secretary.

sentences.zh: 及懷文得罪被繫，沖兄弟行謝，情哀貌苦，見者傷之。

translations.literal: When Huaiwen offended and was imprisoned, Chong and his brothers went to plead; emotion was sorrowful and face bitter—viewers were moved.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaiwen fell into guilt and was bound, Chong and his brothers went to beg mercy, grief in their voices and ruin on their faces, and all who saw them wept.

sentences.zh: 柳元景欲救懷文，言于帝曰：「沈懷文三子塗炭不可見，願陛下速正其罪。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjing wished to save Huaiwen and spoke to the emperor, saying: 「Shen Huaiwen's three sons are in charcoal—unbearable to see; I beg Your Majesty quickly to rectify his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing tried to save Huaiwen and told the emperor, 「Shen Huaiwen's three sons are in the fire—no eye can bear them; let Your Majesty settle his case at once.

sentences.zh: 」帝竟殺之。

translations.literal: 」The emperor in the end killed him.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor killed him all the same.

sentences.zh: 元景爲之嘆息。

translations.literal: Yuanjing sighed for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing mourned it in silence.

sentences.zh: 沖兄弟以此知名。

translations.literal: Chong and his brothers became famous because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and his brothers won their fame from that hour.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，以母老家貧，啓明帝得爲永興令。

translations.literal: At the opening of Taishi, because his mother was old and his home poor, he memorialized Ming Emperor and obtained the post of Magistrate of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Taishi began, his mother was old and his house was poor; he petitioned Emperor Ming and was given Yongxing magistrate.

sentences.zh: 遷巴陵王主簿，除尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to Prince of Baling's chief clerk and made Secretariat Hall Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became the Prince of Baling's chief clerk, then secretariat hall attendant.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，出爲晉安王安西記室參軍，還爲司徒主簿，山陰令，轉司徒錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang period he was sent out as Prince of Jin'an's Pacification of the West secretary, returned as Situ chief clerk and Magistrate of Shanyin, and transferred to Situ recorder staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuankang he went out as secretary on the Prince of Jin'an's pacification of the west, came back as Situ chief clerk and magistrate of Shanyin, then became Situ recorder.

sentences.zh: 世祖爲江州，沖爲征虜長史、尋陽太守，甚見委遇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was in Jiangzhou, Chong was Pacification of the Distant Foe chief aide and Grand Administrator of Xunyang, and was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xiaowu held Jiangzhou, Chong served as pacification-of-the-distant-foe chief aide and grand administrator of Xunyang, and was deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 世祖還都，使沖行府、州事。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu returned to the capital, he had Chong act for headquarters and province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu came back to the capital he left Chong to run headquarters and provincial business.

sentences.zh: 遷領軍長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Army Leader chief aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief aide of the army leader.

sentences.zh: 建元初，轉驃騎諮議參軍，領錄事，未及到任，轉黃門郎，仍遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: At the opening of Jianyuan he was transferred to Rapid Cavalry adviser staff officer and led recorder duties; before he reached the post he was transferred to Yellow Gate Officer, then promoted to Crown Prince Central Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianyuan opened he was made rapid-cavalry adviser and put in charge of recording; before he took up the post he was made yellow gate officer, then crown prince central attendant.

sentences.zh: 世祖在東宮，待以恩舊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was in the Eastern Palace, he treated him as an old favor.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiaowu was still heir, he treated Chong as an old friend of the house.

sentences.zh: 及卽位，轉御史中丞，侍中。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Chong was transferred to Censor-in-Chief and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, the emperor moved Chong to censor-in-chief and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 冠軍廬陵王子卿爲郢州，以沖爲長史、輔國將軍、江夏內史，行府、州事。

translations.literal: The crown-prince's son of Luling, prince of Yingzhou, had Chong as chief clerk, assisting-state general, and Jiangxia interior minister, acting on headquarters and province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince's son of Luling held Yingzhou, Chong served as his chief clerk, assisting-state general, and Jiangxia interior minister, running headquarters and provincial business.

sentences.zh: 隨府轉爲安西長史、南郡內史，行荊州府事，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Following the headquarters he became Anxi chief clerk and Nan commandery interior minister, acting on Jingzhou headquarters affairs; his generalship stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the headquarters west, became Anxi chief clerk and Nan commandery interior minister, and ran Jingzhou headquarters affairs; his general's title was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 永明四年，徵爲五兵尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming he was summoned as Minister of the Five Arms.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming's fourth year he was recalled as minister of the five arms.

sentences.zh: 沖與兄淡、淵名譽有優劣，世號爲「𦝫鼓兄弟。

translations.literal: Chong and his elder brothers Dan and Yuan had reputations of varying excellence; the world called them 「the Leather-Drum Brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and his elder brothers Dan and Yuan won unequal renown; the age nicknamed them 「the Leather-Drum Brothers.

sentences.zh: 」淡、淵竝歷御史中丞，兄弟三人皆爲司直，晉、宋未有也。

translations.literal: 」Dan and Yuan both served as censor-in-chief; three brothers all held the post of straight investigator—unprecedented under Jin and Song.
translations.idiomatic: 」Dan and Yuan had both been censor-in-chief; never under Jin or Song had three brothers all worn the straight investigator's seal.

sentences.zh: 中丞案裁之職，被憲者多結怨。

translations.literal: The censor's duty of judging cases meant many who fell under the statutes bore lasting grudges.
translations.idiomatic: The censor's bench cuts deep: most men the statutes touched nursed a grudge afterward.

sentences.zh: 淵永明中彈吳興太守袁彖，建武中彖從弟昂爲中丞，到官數日，奏彈淵子繢父在僦白幰車，免官禁錮。

translations.literal: In Yongming Yuan impeached Yuan Yi, grand administrator of Wu commandery; in Jianwu Yi's cousin's son Ang became censor, and within days of taking office memorialized against Yuan's son Hui because his father rode in a rented white-canopy carriage—Hui was dismissed and forbidden from office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming, Yuan impeached Yuan Yi, grand administrator of Wu; in Jianwu, Yi's cousin's son Ang took the censor's seat and, within days, struck at Yuan's son Hui for letting his father travel in a hired white-canopy carriage—Hui was cashiered and barred from office.

sentences.zh: 沖母孔氏在東，鄰家失火，疑爲人所焚爇，大呼曰：「我三兒皆作御史中丞，與人豈有善者！」

translations.literal: Chong's mother, of the Kong clan, was in the east; a neighbor's house caught fire and she suspected arson, crying out: 「My three sons are all censor-in-chief—when have we ever dealt kindly with anyone!」
translations.idiomatic: Chong's mother Kong lived in the east. When a neighbor's house burned she cried arson: 「All three of my sons have been censor-in-chief—do you think this family ever did anyone a kindness?」

sentences.zh: 世祖方欲任沖，沖西下至南州而卒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was just about to employ Chong when Chong went west to the southern provinces and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was on the verge of giving Chong greater trust when Chong went west toward the southern provinces and died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 時年五十一。

translations.literal: He was fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 上甚惜之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 喪還，詔曰：「沖喪柩至止，惻愴良深。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, an edict said: 「Chong's bier has reached its halt; my sorrow is profound.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin came home, an edict ran: 「Now that Chong's bier has halted, my grief cuts deep.

sentences.zh: 以其昔在南蕃，特兼憫悼。

translations.literal: Because he once served in the southern marches, I add special pity.」
translations.idiomatic: He once held the southern marches, and I grant him a further measure of pity.」

sentences.zh: 」車駕出臨沖喪，詔曰：「沖貞詳閒理，志局淹正。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage went out to attend Chong's mourning; an edict said: 「Chong was upright, thorough, and versed in principle; his aims were broad and his conduct correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went in person to Chong's mourning; the edict said: 「Chong was upright and exact in principle, his vision wide and his bearing straight.

sentences.zh: 誠著蕃朝，績彰出守。

translations.literal: His loyalty showed in the southern court; his achievements shone in office outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty marked him in the southern court; achievement marked him in posts beyond the capital.

sentences.zh: 不幸早世，朕甚悼之。

translations.literal: His early death is a bitter loss; I grieve deeply.」
translations.idiomatic: To lose him young is bitter grief, and I mourn him deeply.」

sentences.zh: 」追贈太常，諡曰恭子。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand Minister of Ceremonies; his posthumous title was Gongzi, the Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand minister of ceremonies, with the posthumous name Gongzi, the Reverent.

sentences.zh: 庾杲之

translations.literal: Yu Gaozhi
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gaozhi

sentences.zh: 庾杲之字景行，新野人也。

translations.literal: Yu Gaozhi, styled Jingxing, was a native of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gaozhi, styled Jingxing, came from Xinye.

sentences.zh: 祖深之，雍州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shenzhi was governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shenzhi had been governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 父粲，司空參軍。

translations.literal: His father Can was an aide in the ministry of works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Can had served as an aide in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 杲之少而貞立，學涉文義。

translations.literal: Gaozhi from youth was upright and firm, and his studies ranged through literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Gaozhi stood upright and unbending, and he ranged through letters and moral argument.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請，巴陵王-{征}-西參軍。

translations.literal: He began office as a court gentleman, staff officer on the Prince of Baling's west-expedition army.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a court gentleman and staff officer on the Prince of Baling's west-expedition army.

sentences.zh: 郢州舉秀才，除晉熙王鎮西外兵參軍，世祖徵虜府功曹，尚書駕部郎。

translations.literal: Yingzhou nominated him as xiucai; he was made outer military aide to the Prince of Jinxi's army-protector staff, merit recorder on the heir apparent's campaign-against-barbarians headquarters, and gentleman of the ministry chariot-and-horse bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou nominated him as xiucai; he became outer military aide on the Prince of Jinxi's army-protector staff, merit recorder on the heir apparent's pacification headquarters, and gentleman of the chariot-and-horse bureau.

sentences.zh: 清貧自業，食唯有韭菹、𤅢韭、生韭雜菜，或戲之曰：「誰謂庾郎貧，食鮭常有二十七種。

translations.literal: Poor and self-reliant, his fare was only chive pickle, vinegared chives, raw chives, and mixed vegetables; someone jested: 「Who says Minister Yu is poor? When he eats salmon there are always twenty-seven kinds.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in poverty by choice; his table held only chive pickle, vinegared chives, raw chives, and humble greens. A wit said: 「Who calls Minister Yu poor? When he dines on salmon he still has twenty-seven kinds.

sentences.zh: 」言三九也。

translations.literal: 」—meaning three times nine.
translations.idiomatic: 」—three dishes, three nines.

sentences.zh: 仍爲世祖撫軍中軍記室，遷員外散騎常侍，正員郎，遷中書郎，領荊、湘二州中正。

translations.literal: He then became recorder on the heir apparent's pacification army and central army, was promoted to supernumerary regular cavalier attendant, then full attendant, was moved to secretariat gentleman, and held the rectifier posts for Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He became recorder on the heir apparent's pacification and central armies, rose to supernumerary regular cavalier attendant, then full attendant, was moved to secretariat gentleman, and held the rectifier posts for Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書左丞，常侍、領中正如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left vice director of the ministry of works; regular attendant and rectifier stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left vice director of the ministry of works while keeping his regular attendant and rectifier posts.

sentences.zh: 出爲王儉衛軍長史，時人呼入儉府爲芙蓉池。

translations.literal: He went out as chief clerk on Wang Jian's guard-army staff; men of the day called entering Jian's office 「the Lotus Pond.」
translations.idiomatic: He went out as chief clerk on Wang Jian's guard-army staff; contemporaries called service in Jian's house 「the Lotus Pond.」

sentences.zh: 儉謂人曰：「昔袁公作衛軍，欲用我爲長史，雖不獲就，要是意向如此。

translations.literal: Jian told others: 「In the past Yuan Gong held the guard army and wished to make me chief clerk; though I did not take it, that was the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jian told others: 「When Yuan Gong ran the guard army he wanted me as chief clerk; I never took the post, but the wish was plain.

sentences.zh: 今亦應須如我輩人也。

translations.literal: Now he should likewise have men of our sort.」
translations.idiomatic: Now he ought to have men of our stamp again.」

sentences.zh: 」乃用杲之。

translations.literal: And so Gaozhi was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: So Gaozhi was chosen.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門郎，兼御史中丞，尋卽正。

translations.literal: He was moved to gentleman at the Yellow Gate, with concurrent censor-in-chief; soon he held the censorate in full.
translations.idiomatic: He was made gentleman at the Yellow Gate and acting censor-in-chief; before long the censorate was his in full.

sentences.zh: 杲之風範和潤，善音吐。

translations.literal: Gaozhi's bearing was mild and harmonious, and he was skilled in clear delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhi's manner was mild and harmonious, and his speech was beautifully clear.

sentences.zh: 世祖令對虜使，兼侍中。

translations.literal: The heir apparent ordered him to face the barbarian envoys, with added rank as attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent had him receive the barbarian envoys, with added rank as attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 上每嘆其風器之美，王儉在座，曰：「杲之爲蟬冕所照，更生風采。

translations.literal: The emperor often sighed over the beauty of his presence; Wang Jian, seated nearby, said: 「When Gaozhi's cicada crown catches the imperial light, his bearing shines all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often sighed over the grace of his person; Wang Jian, seated beside him, said: 「Set Gaozhi's cicada crown under the throne's radiance and his bearing only grows brighter.

sentences.zh: 陛下故當與其卽眞。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to grant him the real appointment.」
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should give him the full post at last.」

sentences.zh: 」帝意未用也。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind had not yet settled on it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not yet made up his mind.

sentences.zh: 永明中，諸王年少，不得妄與人接，敕杲之與濟陽江淹五日一詣諸王，使申游好。

translations.literal: In Yongming the princes were young and might not receive visitors at will; the throne ordered Gaozhi and Jiang Yan of Jiyang to call on the princes every five days, so that friendly ties might be kept.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming the princes were still young and might not receive visitors freely; the court ordered Gaozhi and Jiang Yan of Jiyang to call on them every five days and keep cordial ties alive.

sentences.zh: 尋又遷廬陵王中軍長史，遷尚書吏部郎，參大選事。

translations.literal: Soon he was again moved to chief clerk on the Prince of Luling's central army, then to director of the ministry of personnel, sharing charge of the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became chief clerk on the Prince of Luling's central army, then director of the ministry of personnel, sharing charge of the great selection.

sentences.zh: 轉太子右衛率，加通直常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right commander of the heir apparent's guard, with added rank as unimpeded regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made right commander of the heir apparent's guard, with added rank as unimpeded regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died.

sentences.zh: 臨終上表曰：「臣昨夜及旦，更增氣疾，自省綿痼，頃刻危殆，無容復臥。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he submitted a memorial: 「Last night and this morning my breath-sickness grew worse; seeing my long illness, I am in peril from moment to moment and can no longer lie abed.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he submitted a memorial: 「Last night and this dawn my breath-sickness worsened; I know this chronic ailment, and moment by moment I edge toward death—I can no longer keep to my couch.

sentences.zh: 任居隆顯，玷塵明世，乞解所忝，待終私庭。

translations.literal: My post is lofty and bright, yet I stain a luminous age; I beg to be released from what I hold and await the end in my own house.
translations.idiomatic: I hold a lofty, glaring post and soil a bright reign; I beg release from my offices and leave to meet the end in my own hall.

sentences.zh: 臣以凡庸，謬徼昌運，獎擢之厚，千載難逢。

translations.literal: I am a common mediocrity who wrongly caught a prosperous age; the favor shown me is a bounty met once in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: I am a common mediocrity who stumbled into a prosperous age; the favor the throne has shown me comes once in a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 且年逾知命，志事榮顯，脩夭有分，無所厝言。

translations.literal: I have already passed the age of knowing mandate; my aims were honor and eminence; length of life has its portion, and I have nothing left to say.
translations.idiomatic: I have already passed the age of knowing Heaven's mandate; I sought honor and a shining name; life and death have their measure, and I have no further plea.

sentences.zh: 若天鑒微誠，暫借餘歷，傾宗殞元，陳力無遠。

translations.literal: If Heaven looks on my slight sincerity and lends me a little more time, I would spend my clan and give my life, serving with all my strength and never from afar.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven reads my slight sincerity and grants me a little more time, I would spend house and kin and lay down my life, serving with all my strength and never at a distance.

sentences.zh: 仰違庭闕，伏枕鯁戀。

translations.literal: I look up and turn from the palace court; prostrate on my pillow, my throat tight with longing.
translations.idiomatic: I look up and leave the palace gate behind; pillow-bound, my throat knots with longing.

sentences.zh: 送貂蟬及章。

translations.literal: He sent in his cicada crown and seal.
translations.idiomatic: He sent in his cicada crown and seal of office.

sentences.zh: 」詔不許。

translations.literal: 」The edict did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: 」The throne would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 杲之歷在上府，以文學見遇。

translations.literal: Gaozhi had long served in the upper offices and was favored for his literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhi had risen through the great households and won notice for letters.

sentences.zh: 上造崇虛館，使爲碑文。

translations.literal: The emperor built the Chongxu Pavilion and had him compose its memorial inscription.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raised the Chongxu Pavilion and set him to write the stone.

sentences.zh: 卒時年五十一，上甚惜之。

translations.literal: When he died he was fifty-one; the emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-one, and the throne mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 諡曰貞子。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Master Upright.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Zhenzi, Master Upright.

sentences.zh: 時會稽孔廣，字淹源，亦美姿制。

translations.literal: At the time Kong Guang of Kuaiji, styled Yanyuan, also had a fine bearing.
translations.idiomatic: About then Kong Guang of Kuaiji, styled Yanyuan, was likewise praised for his looks.

sentences.zh: 歷州治中，卒。

translations.literal: He served as a province chief clerk and died.
translations.idiomatic: He held a provincial chief clerkship and died.

sentences.zh: 王諶

translations.literal: Wang Chen
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen

sentences.zh: 王諶字仲和，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chen, styled Zhonghe, was a man of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen, styled Zhonghe, came from Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 祖萬慶，員外常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wanging was an outer regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wanging served as outer regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 父元閔，護軍司馬。

translations.literal: His father Yuanmin was guard-army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanmin was marshal of the guard army.

sentences.zh: 宋大明中，沈曇慶爲徐州，辟諶爲迎主簿，又爲州迎從事，湘東王國常侍，鎮北行參軍，州、國、府主皆宋明帝也。

translations.literal: In Song's Daming era, when Shen Tanqing was in Xuzhou, Chen was summoned as reception chief clerk, then made reception staff officer for the province, constant attendant in the Prince of Xiangdong's kingdom, and northern campaign staff officer—all three lords, province, kingdom, and princely house, were Emperor Ming of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song's Daming reign Shen Tanqing held Xuzhou and called Chen in as reception chief clerk, then reception staff officer, constant attendant in the Prince of Xiangdong's household, and northern-campaign staff officer—province, kingdom, and princely seat alike belonged to Emperor Ming of Song.

sentences.zh: 除義陽王征北行參軍，又除度明帝衛軍府。

translations.literal: He was made staff officer on the Prince of Yiyang's northern campaign; he was also appointed to Emperor Ming's guard-army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He became staff officer on the Prince of Yiyang's northern campaign, then entered Emperor Ming's guard-army staff.

sentences.zh: 諶有學義，累爲帝蕃佐。

translations.literal: Chen had learning and principle and repeatedly served as the emperor's household aide.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was learned and upright and for years was the emperor's man in the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 及卽位，除司徒參軍，帶薛令，兼中書舍人，見親遇，常在左右。

translations.literal: When Ming took the throne, Chen was made secretariat staff officer with concurrent magistrate of Xue, also secretariat gentleman, and was favored and kept at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming ascended, Chen was made a secretariat staff officer with concurrent magistrate of Xue and secretariat gentleman, kept close and favored at the throne's side.

sentences.zh: 諶見帝所行慘僻，屢諫不從，請退，坐此見怒，繫尚方，少日出。

translations.literal: Chen saw the emperor's conduct cruel and perverse; he remonstrated again and again without being heeded, asked to withdraw, and for this was enraged, bound in the Imperial Workshop, and released after a few days.
translations.idiomatic: Chen watched the emperor grow cruel and strange; he pleaded again and again and was not heard, asked to leave office, and for it was thrown into the Imperial Workshop for a few days before release.

sentences.zh: 尋除尚書殿中郎，徙記室參軍，正員郎，薛令如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was made hall attendant in the Masters of Writing, moved to recorder staff officer, regular officer, and magistrate of Xue as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was hall attendant in the Masters of Writing, then recorder, regular officer, still magistrate of Xue.

sentences.zh: 遷兼中書郎，晉平王驃騎板諮議，出爲湘東太守，秩中二千石，未拜，坐公事免。

translations.literal: He was promoted to concurrent secretariat officer, staff adviser on the Prince of Jinping's rapid-cavalry staff, and sent out as grand administrator of Xiangdong at the rank of two thousand shi; before he took up the post he was dismissed for a public matter.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to concurrent secretariat officer and staff adviser on the Prince of Jinping's rapid-cavalry command, then was sent out as grand administrator of Xiangdong at two-thousand-shi rank; before he took the seal he was removed for an official fault.

sentences.zh: 復爲桂陽王驃騎府諮議參軍，中書郎。

translations.literal: He was again made staff adviser on the Prince of Guiyang's rapid-cavalry staff and secretariat officer.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as staff adviser on the Prince of Guiyang's rapid-cavalry staff and as secretariat officer.

sentences.zh: 明帝好圍棊，置圍棊州邑，以建安王休仁爲圍棊州都大中正，諶與太子右率沈勃、尚書水部郎庾珪之、彭城丞王抗四人爲小中正，朝請褚思庄、傅楚之爲清定訪問。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming loved weiqi and established a weiqi prefecture and districts; he made the Prince of Jian'an, Xiuren, grand rectifier of the Weiqi Province, with Chen, the crown prince's right leader Shen Bo, Masters of Writing waters-section officer Yu Guizhi, and Pengcheng aide Wang Kang as lesser rectifiers, and court gentlemen Chu Sizhuang and Fu Chuzhi as clarification inquirers.
translations.idiomatic: Ming loved weiqi and set up a weiqi province with its own ranks; he named the Prince of Jian'an, Xiuren, grand rectifier of Weiqi Province, with Chen, the crown prince's right leader Shen Bo, waters-section officer Yu Guizhi, and Pengcheng aide Wang Kang as lesser rectifiers, and court gentlemen Chu Sizhuang and Fu Chuzhi to settle disputes.

sentences.zh: 出爲臨川內史，還爲尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was sent out as interior administrator of Linchuan and returned as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as interior administrator of Linchuan and came back as left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官領東觀祭酒，卽明帝所置總明觀也。

translations.literal: Before long, in his existing office, he headed the Eastern Lodge sacrifice office—the Zongming Observatory Ming had founded.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, keeping his post, he headed the Eastern Lodge sacrifice office, the Zongming Observatory Ming had raised.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門，轉正員常侍，輔國將軍，江夏王右軍長史，冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to Yellow Gate, then regular attendant, aide to the state, staff officer to the Prince of Jiangxia's right army, and champion general.
translations.idiomatic: He became yellow gate officer, then regular attendant, aide to the state, staff officer on the Prince of Jiangxia's right army, and champion general.

sentences.zh: 轉給事中，廷尉卿，未拜。

translations.literal: He was transferred to attendant within the gates and made minister of justice; he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant within the gates and minister of justice, but never took the seal.

sentences.zh: 建元中，武陵王曄爲會稽，以諶爲征虜長史行事，冠軍如故。

translations.literal: In Jianyuan, when the Prince of Wuling, Ye, held Kuaiji, Chen was made acting chief staff officer on the Pacify-the-Barbarians command, champion general as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan, when the Prince of Wuling, Ye, governed Kuaiji, Chen was acting chief staff officer on the pacify-the-barbarians command, still champion general.

sentences.zh: 永明初，遷豫章王太尉司馬，將軍如故。

translations.literal: At the opening of Yongming he was moved to grand marshal staff officer to the Prince of Yuzhang; his generalship stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongming began he became grand marshal staff officer to the Prince of Yuzhang, his generalship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 世祖與諶相遇於宋明之世，欲委任，爲輔國將軍、晉安王南中郎長史、淮南太守，行府、州事。

translations.literal: The Shizu emperor had known Chen in Ming of Song's time and wished to entrust him; he was made aide to the state, chief staff officer to the Prince of Jin'an's southern center, and grand administrator of Huainan, acting for headquarters and province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi had known Chen in Emperor Ming of Song's reign and meant to use him well: aide to the state, chief staff officer to the Prince of Jin'an's southern center, grand administrator of Huainan, running headquarters and province.

sentences.zh: 五年，除黃門郎，領驍騎將軍，遷太子中庶子，驍騎如故。

translations.literal: In year five he was made Yellow Gate Officer, with added rank as valiant cavalry general, moved to crown prince central attendant, valiant cavalry as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he was yellow gate officer with added valiant cavalry general, then crown prince central attendant, valiant cavalry unchanged.

sentences.zh: 諶貞正和謹，朝廷稱爲善人，多與之厚。

translations.literal: Chen was upright, harmonious, and careful; the court called him a good man, and many drew close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was upright, even-tempered, and careful; the court named him a good man, and many kept him near.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉冠軍將軍、長沙王車騎長史，徙廬陵王中軍長史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In year eight he was moved to champion general and chief staff officer to the Prince of Changsha's chariot-and-cavalry command, then staff officer on the Prince of Luling's central army; his generalship stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he became champion general and chief staff officer to the Prince of Changsha's chariot-and-cavalry command, then staff officer on the Prince of Luling's central army, his generalship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 西陽王子明在南兖州，長史沈憲去職，上復徙諶爲征虜長史，行南兖府、州事，將軍如故。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiyang, Ziming, was in Southern Yanzhou; when chief staff officer Shen Xian left office, the emperor moved Chen again to chief staff officer on the Pacify-the-Barbarians command, acting for the southern Yan headquarters and province; his generalship stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiyang, Ziming, held Southern Yanzhou; when chief staff officer Shen Xian quit, the emperor set Chen again as pacify-the-barbarians chief staff officer, acting for headquarters and province, generalship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 諶少貧，嘗自紡績，及通貴後，每爲人說之，世稱其志達。

translations.literal: Chen had been poor in youth and once spun thread himself; after he rose to wealth he still told people of it, and the age praised his ambition fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Chen was poor and spun thread with his own hands; even after he grew rich he still told the story, and men praised him for ambition that had crossed poverty.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒。

translations.literal: In year nine he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he died.

sentences.zh: 年六十九。

translations.literal: He was sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-nine.

translations.literal: Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：鶉居鷇飲，裁樹司牧，板籍之起，尚未分民，所以愛字之義深，納隍之意重也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When men lived like quail in their nests and drank like fledglings, they only then planted marker trees and appointed herdsmen; when household registers arose, the people had not yet been divided—hence the deep meaning of cherishing the folk and the weight of receiving the drowning from the moat.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: In the age when men nested like quail and drank like unfledged birds, they only then set boundary trees and named overseers; when board registers began, the people were not yet carved into classes—so the duty to cherish them ran deep, and the heart to pull the drowning from the moat weighed heavy.

sentences.zh: 季世以後，務盡民力，量財品賦，以自奉養。

translations.literal: After the late age, the state exhausted the people's strength, measured wealth and graded levies, to feed itself.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynasty declined, rulers drained the people's strength, tallied goods and graded taxes, to keep their own tables full.

sentences.zh: 下窮而上不卹，世澆而事愈變。

translations.literal: Below were destitute while above showed no pity; the age grew thin and affairs changed the faster.
translations.idiomatic: The poor sank lower while the throne looked away; the world thinned out and fraud changed shape year by year.

sentences.zh: 故有竊名簿閥，忍賊肌膚，生濫死乖，趨避繩網。

translations.literal: Hence men stole names on the registers, endured flaying the people's skin, registered the living falsely and misrecorded the dead, and scrambled to dodge the net of law.
translations.idiomatic: So men stole names on the household rolls, bore the cost of skinning the people, let the living swell the lists while the dead went astray, and dodged through holes in the law.

sentences.zh: 積虛累謬，已數十年，欺蔽相容，官民共有，爲國之道，良宜矯革。

translations.literal: Falsehoods piled for decades; deceit sheltered deceit, and officials and people shared the game—for the way of governing a realm, this should be sternly reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Lies had stacked for decades; fraud covered fraud, and magistrate and commoner played the same trick—for a state's health, this must be cut back hard.

sentences.zh: 若令優役輕徭，則斯詐自弭；

translations.literal: If light corvée and easy levies were ordered, this trickery would itself die down;
translations.idiomatic: Ease the labor and lighten the tax, and the trickery dies on its own;

sentences.zh: 明糾羣吏，則茲偽不行。

translations.literal: if the clerks were clearly disciplined, this forgery would not stand.
translations.idiomatic: discipline the clerks in the open, and the forgery cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 空閱舊文，徒成民幸。

translations.literal: To read old documents in vain only breeds the people's luck.
translations.idiomatic: To leaf through old papers and do nothing only teaches the people to gamble on luck.

sentences.zh: 是以崔琰之譏魏武，謝安之論京師。

translations.literal: Hence Cui Yan's rebuke of Cao Cao and Xie An's argument over the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Cui Yan reproached Cao Cao, and Xie An argued over the capital.

sentences.zh: 斷民之難，豈直遠在周世哉？

translations.literal: The hardship of cutting the people off—is it only far back in the Zhou age?
translations.idiomatic: The pain of drafting and draining the people—was it only the Zhou dynasty that knew it?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：玩之止足，爲論未光。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Wanzhi knew sufficiency—yet his discourse did not shine.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium runs: Wanzhi knew when he had enough—yet his argument never caught the light.

sentences.zh: 劉休善筮，安臥南湘。

translations.literal: Liu Xiu was skilled at the stalks and rested at peace in south Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiu read the yarrow well and slept easy in south Xiang.

sentences.zh: 沖獲時譽，杲信圭璋。

translations.literal: Chong won the age's praise; Gaozhi was trusted like jade and scepter.
translations.idiomatic: Chong drew the age's praise; Gaozhi stood in trust like jade tablet and scepter.

sentences.zh: 諶惟舊序，並用興王。

translations.literal: Chen by old order—all were used to raise the kings.
translations.idiomatic: Chen by long standing—all alike helped lift the throne.
